_note: Machine-readable map of the SOC 1000 first-year course. scripts/verify_course.py --course 1000 checks the prose against this file: 15 modules, homework per module, anchors that really exist on the reference site. SOC 1000 teaches the intro toolkit through A Different World; it is NOT a watered-down SOC 4150.

course.title: Introduction to Sociology: Reading the Social World through A Different World

outcomes.LO1: Define and apply the sociological imagination; distinguish personal troubles from public issues
outcomes.LO2: Explain and apply core concepts (culture, socialization, groups, deviance, stratification, race, gender, institutions) to a concrete case
outcomes.LO3: Distinguish structure and agency, and identify both in a social scene
outcomes.LO4: Read a popular media text sociologically, separating documented fact from interpretation
outcomes.LO5: Use evidence to evaluate an empirical claim about social life
outcomes.LO6: Connect the A Different World case to general sociological concepts

core_readings: C. Wright Mills, The Sociological Imagination (1959), ch. 1
